metadata.description: Small FPGA system that classifies one INT8 28x28 MNIST digit with a pre-trained 784→128→10 MLP, running firmware on an in-house RV32I+Zmmul 5-stage core that offloads dot product, bias, requantize and ReLU to an in-house Zve32x VPU (VLEN 128, 4 lanes). Includes IMEM/DMEM, APB4 MMIO to a generated CSR block, UART TX and a host load port.

requirements.text: The core shall implement RV32I base instructions (arithmetic/logic, lui, auipc, jumps, branches, lb lh lw lbu lhu sb sh sw) with a 5-stage in-order pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) at one instruction per cycle absent hazards.
The core shall implement `mul` (Zmmul) returning the low 32 bits of the signed product and shall treat `div`, `divu`, `rem`, `remu` and `mulh*` as illegal instructions.

The core shall resolve branches and jumps in EX, predict not-taken, and flush IF/ID when taken; it shall forward EX/MEM→EX and MEM/WB→EX, and insert exactly 1 bubble for a load followed by an immediate use.

A wrong-path instruction flushed by a taken branch or jump before it commits shall have no effect: an illegal instruction or `ebreak` in that shadow shall not halt the core and shall not set `o_err_illegal` or `sts.err`.
The VPU shall execute `vsetvli`, `vsetivli` (including `vsetvli zero,zero,...`) with vl = min(AVL, VLMAX), VLMAX = (PARA_VLEN/SEW) x LMUL, and return vl through `o_resp_rd_data`.
The VPU shall execute `vle8.v`, `vse8.v`, `vle32.v`, `vse32.v` as unit-stride accesses of exactly vl elements, leaving tail elements and non-written bytes unchanged (byte-enable on stores).
The VPU shall execute `vwmul.vv` (INT8xINT8→INT16 signed, including -128 x -128 = 16384) writing a register pair.

The VPU shall execute `vwredsum.vs` accumulating signed INT16 elements into a signed INT32 without overflow for up to 784 elements and write the sum plus the initial scalar (vs1[0]) to element 0 of the destination.

The VPU shall execute `vadd.vv/vx`, `vsra.vi/vx`, `vmax.vx`, `vnclip.wi/wx`, `vmv.v.x`, `vmv.s.x`, `vmv.x.s`; `vnclip` shall saturate to the signed range of the destination element width with no wrap-around ([-32768, 32767] for 32→16, [-128, 127] for 16→8), using shift[4:0] for 32→16 and shift[3:0] for 16→8; `vsra` shall mask the shift amount to log2(SEW) bits and `vmv.x.s` shall sign-extend the element to 32 bits (RVV 1.0 semantics, also at SEW = 8); results shall match the golden model bit-for-bit.
On a vector instruction the CPU shall send the instruction and rs1/rs2 values to the VPU and stall the whole pipeline until `o_resp_done`; one vector instruction shall execute at a time.

Every vector command, including `vsetvli`/`vsetivli`, shall pass through all six `m_vpu_ctrl` states (IDLE, DEC, RD, EXEC, WB, DONE), so the latency from command start to `o_resp_done` shall be at least 5 cycles.
`m_imem` shall provide 32 KB (8192 x 32) with a synchronous 1-cycle read.
`m_dmem` shall provide 256 KB, single port, PARA_VLEN bits wide, with byte enable and registered read data valid in the cycle after the read.
`m_uart` shall transmit one byte at 8N1 with baud divisor `uart_cfg.baud_div` when `uart_tx.send` is written 1, assert `uart_tx.busy` during transmission, and clear `send` when it takes the byte.

`m_vpu_perf` shall count `i_clk_core` cycles from vector-instruction start to done and present the value on `i_cycles_cnt`, which feeds `cycles.cnt`; the window is inclusive (counting starts at 1 in the cycle after the start pulse, so the start cycle is counted, and includes the done-pulse cycle); `m_csr_min` is a separate CPU-side counter and shall not feed `cycles.cnt`.
The system shall classify the image with a result bit-identical (logits and label) to the golden model for the delivered firmware and weights.
The memory map shall be IMEM 0x0000_0000 (32 KB), DMEM 0x1000_0000 (256 KB), MMIO 0x2000_0000 (4 KB); `m_soc_bus` shall decode by address and mux the VPU and CPU memory ports.

`m_apb_master` shall convert CPU data-bus accesses to the MMIO region into APB SETUP/ACCESS cycles and hold `i_dmem_ack` low until PREADY; for writes it shall forward the CPU byte enables to PSTRB and keep the low 2 address bits on PADDR, with PSTRB = 4'b1111 only for an aligned full-word access.

MMIO reads shall never raise PSLVERR (no PSTRB is forwarded for reads); a sub-word (`lb`, `lh`, `lbu`, `lhu`) or misaligned `lw` read of MMIO shall complete without hanging or halting the core, and its data and `sts.err` are not specified.
When PSLVERR is sampled with PREADY = 1, `m_apb_master` shall drive a 1-cycle pulse (`o_sts_err_set`) to the CSR hardware-write port of `sts.err`; the CPU shall see a normal `i_dmem_ack`.

When `i_ld_en` = 0, the `m_soc_bus` DMEM port shall pass to `m_dmem` unchanged through a combinational 2:1 mux (no added cycle), the IMEM write enable shall be 0 and other `i_ld_*` inputs shall be ignored.
When `i_ld_en` = 1 and `i_ld_req` = 1 an IMEM write at `i_ld_addr[31:15]` = 0 shall write the whole word at index `i_ld_addr[14:2]` at that rising edge, ignoring `i_ld_byte_en`.

A DMEM access (`i_ld_addr[31:18]` = 14'h0400) shall address 32-bit lane `i_ld_addr[LB-1:2]` of row `i_ld_addr[17:LB]` (LB = log2(PARA_VLEN/8)) and a write shall change exactly the bytes enabled by `i_ld_byte_en`.

A host read shall return data on `o_ld_rd_data` exactly 1 cycle after the request; a read of IMEM, MMIO or an unmapped address shall return 0, and a write to MMIO or an unmapped address shall change nothing.
The host port shall accept back-to-back accesses every cycle with no handshake.
`i_ld_en` shall be 0 at every rising edge of `i_clk_core` where `i_rst_n_core` = 1; the testbench shall check this with an assertion.
`m_soc_csr` shall be connected with `i_slverr_en` = 1 and `i_protect_en` = 0 and be generated with Asynchronous = 0.

An access to an unimplemented offset inside the 4 KB MMIO window shall read 0 and ignore a write, shall not hang the core and shall not change any defined register; `sts.err` is not specified for such accesses.

`m_soc_top` shall provide the ports i_clk_core (1), i_rst_n_core (1), i_start_req (1), o_sts_done (1), o_result_label (4), o_uart_tx (1), o_err_illegal (1), o_halt (1), i_ld_en (1), i_ld_req (1), i_ld_wr_en (1), i_ld_addr (32), i_ld_byte_en (4), i_ld_wr_data (32), o_ld_rd_data (32); the port list shall be the same in every configuration.
A level 1 on `i_start_req` for at least 1 cycle shall set `ctrl.start` through the `i_hw_wdata_ctrl_start`/`i_hw_we_ctrl_start` ports of `m_soc_csr`; firmware clears it.
The status outputs `o_err_illegal`, `o_halt`, `o_sts_done` and `o_result_label` shall be registered level outputs in the core domain and reset to 0; `o_uart_tx` shall reset to 1 (idle high).

`m_apb_master` shall run the APB transfer as SETUP then ACCESS: `o_apb_psel` high from SETUP through ACCESS, `o_apb_penable` high in ACCESS only, address/control/write data stable from SETUP until completion; for writes `o_apb_pstrb` shall carry the CPU byte enables (4'b1111 only for an aligned full-word access); `o_apb_paddr` shall be the CPU address minus 0x2000_0000 with the low 2 bits being the CPU address bits; `o_apb_pprot` = 0; the transfer completes at the rising edge where `i_apb_pready` = 1 in ACCESS, when `i_apb_prdata` and `i_apb_pslverr` are sampled.
An MMIO access shall take at least 3 cycles (SETUP, ACCESS, plus at least 1 cycle of PREADY latency), and the CPU pipeline shall be stalled until the transfer completes.
`m_apb_master` shall not start a new transfer until the previous one completes (one outstanding transfer).

A CPU→VPU command shall transfer at the rising edge where `i_cmd_valid` = 1 and `o_cmd_ready` = 1; `i_cmd_valid` shall be held with stable `i_cmd_instr`/`i_cmd_rs1_data`/`i_cmd_rs2_data` until then, and `o_resp_done` shall be a 1-cycle pulse.
`o_cmd_ready` shall be asserted only when `m_vpu_ctrl` is in IDLE.

On the VPU memory interface `o_mem_req` shall be held with stable address and data until `i_mem_ack`, and the low log2(PARA_VLEN/8) address bits shall be ignored so that every access is to a PARA_VLEN/8-byte-aligned row.
The CPU and the VPU shall never request DMEM in the same cycle, and the host shall never access DMEM when `i_rst_n_core` = 1.
`x0` of `m_regfile` shall always read 0.

`m_vpu_ctrl` shall step IDLE → DEC (on `i_cmd_valid`) → RD → EXEC (one or more passes, load/store through `m_vpu_lsu`) → WB → DONE (pulse `o_resp_done`) → IDLE, with reset state IDLE and the 2 unused 3-bit codes recovering to IDLE.
`m_vpu_lsu` shall step IDLE → REQ (assert `o_mem_req` with address) → WAIT → DONE (on `i_mem_ack`) → IDLE, with reset state IDLE (2-bit encoding, no unused codes).
The `m_apb_master` (apbm: IDLE, SETUP, ACCESS) and `m_uart` (uart: IDLE, START, DATA, STOP) FSMs shall reset to IDLE and recover to IDLE from unused encodings.
The design shall use a single clock domain `core` (`i_clk_core`) with no CDC and no clock gating.
`i_rst_n_core` shall be asserted asynchronously and released synchronously through `m_rst_sync`.
After reset the PC shall be 0x0000_0000, the pipeline empty, all FSMs in IDLE, `o_halt` and `o_err_illegal` 0.
Reset shall not gate the host port and shall not clear IMEM or DMEM contents.
Firmware `start.S` shall not clear DMEM.
A reset during a running inference shall abort any in-flight instruction or APB transfer and reset the CSR registers and results, while keeping IMEM and DMEM contents.
`PARA_VLEN` shall be 128 or 256 (default 128) and divisible by PARA_LANE_COUNT x LPARA_LANE_W.
`PARA_LANE_COUNT` shall be 1, 2, 4 or 8 (default 4).
Illegal parameter values shall be rejected at elaboration with `$error` in a generate-`if`.
Elaboration constraint C1: PARA_VLEN == 128 || PARA_VLEN == 256.
Elaboration constraint C2: PARA_LANE_COUNT shall be 1, 2, 4 or 8 (a power of 2).
Elaboration constraint C3: PARA_VLEN % (PARA_LANE_COUNT * LPARA_LANE_W) == 0 (LPARA_LANE_W = 32).

The derived local parameters shall be LPARA_LANE_W = 32, LPARA_VREG_COUNT = 32, LPARA_ROW_LB = $clog2(PARA_VLEN/8) and LPARA_VL_W = $clog2(PARA_VLEN/8 + 1), the largest VLMAX being PARA_VLEN/8 (SEW = 8, LMUL = 1).
An illegal instruction shall halt the core (`o_halt` = 1), assert `o_err_illegal` and set `sts.err`; the instruction shall not be dispatched to the VPU.

In the Halted state (entered on an illegal instruction or `ebreak`) the PC shall stop and the pipeline be drained; `o_halt` shall stay 1 until reset, with `o_err_illegal` = 1 if the cause was an illegal instruction and 0 for `ebreak`.

`m_cpu_dec` shall decode the supported Zve32x subset itself, including the SEW and LMUL fields of `vsetvli`/`vsetivli` immediates (only LMUL = 1 and SEW 8, 16, 32 are legal), and shall flag any other OP-V instruction as illegal before dispatch: only the exact forms of REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-008 plus `vwmul.vv` and `vwredsum.vs` are legal, and every other form is illegal, including `vsetvl` (register form), `vwmulu`, `vwredsumu`, `vadd.vi`, `vsra.vv`, `vmax.vv`, `vnclip.wv`, `vwmul.vx`, `vmv.v.v`, `vmv.v.i`, masked forms (vm = 0), `vle16`/`vse16`, and mask, segment, whole-register and fault-only-first loads and stores; the `m_vpu_top` interface has no error response.
A partial (PSTRB != 4'b1111) or misaligned APB write to `m_soc_csr` shall produce PSLVERR and not modify any register; a misaligned MMIO store is a partial write and therefore sets `sts.err`.
`m_lsu` shall let `sb`/`sh` accesses to the MMIO region reach the APB master (not block them), which forwards the CPU byte enables to PSTRB, so that the resulting PSLVERR sets `sts.err`.
A CPU access to an unmapped data address, including the IMEM range (0x0000_0000-0x0000_7FFF), shall return 0 on a read and ignore a write, with no error flag.

When a VPU unit-stride access address is not row-aligned, the VPU shall ignore the low log2(PARA_VLEN/8) address bits and access the aligned row, without raising an error; only the row part of `o_mem_addr` is significant, and `m_vpu_top` may drive the ignored low bits unmodified or cleared (they are not checked).
For vector instructions, elements with index >= vl shall be left unchanged (tail-undisturbed) and the destination registers other than those written shall not change.
`vnclip` shall use rounding mode round-to-nearest-up (vxrm = 0), matching the golden model.
A same-address read-during-write inside `m_dmem` shall return the old data (read-first).

The vector instruction latency shall be multi-cycle and not fixed by this spec beyond the 5-cycle minimum (initiation interval = latency); `vwredsum` reduction latency is also unspecified and only result values are checked.
A UART byte shall take 10 bit times of `baud_div` clocks each (start, 8 data, stop), and `uart_tx.send` shall be cleared when the byte is taken.
The inference time shall be below 1,000,000 cycles per image (target).
The INT8 accuracy on the 10,000 test images shall be at least 96% (golden model).
A taken branch shall cost about 2 cycles of penalty (estimate).
A dot-product iteration (vle8, vle8, vwmul.vv, vwredsum.vs) shall take about 6-10 cycles (goal, not hard).
The design shall target a 200 MHz `i_clk_core` (5 ns) on Arria 10 with Quartus (goal, not hard); closure is claimed only by STA with the SDC in `constraints/`.
All RTL except `m_soc_csr` shall comply with REF-003.

RTL shall contain no `initial` block or `$readmemh`; memory initialization shall use the flow's init file inside the `m_imem`/`m_dmem` wrappers, and simulation shall load memories by testbench hierarchical reference.
Testbenches, models and SVA shall reside in `tb/`, outside the synthesis filelist.
A regression script shall report PASS/FAIL over instruction-, layer- and system-level tests.
`ebreak` shall halt the core (`o_halt` = 1, `o_err_illegal` = 0); `fence` shall execute as a NOP; `ecall` and all CSR and other SYSTEM opcodes shall be illegal instructions.

Vector instructions shall be legal only for these SEW combinations: `vwmul.vv` with SEW = 8 sources and 16-bit results; `vwredsum.vs` with 16-bit source elements and a 32-bit sum, reading element indexes below vl (up to PARA_VLEN/8 elements) from the register pair vs2/vs2+1; `vadd`, `vsra`, `vmax`, `vmv` at SEW = 32 and 8; `vnclip` in the steps 32→16 and 16→8. Any other SEW combination, or a widening-result `vd` that is not an even register, shall be an illegal instruction; only the widening-result `vd` is alignment-checked and an odd `vs2` of a wide source is not checked.

Misaligned scalar loads and stores shall not trap: byte enables and data shall be shifted by addr[1:0] and bytes falling outside the word shall be dropped, with no word-crossing split; a misaligned load shall return word >> (8 x addr[1:0]) with the missing upper bytes zero-filled, then the normal sign or zero extension of the access width.
`m_regfile` shall bypass a same-cycle write-back write to a read port (write-to-read bypass), with `x0` still reading 0.
For `vsetvli zero,zero,...` the VPU shall keep vl and write the new SEW when the setting is legal (LMUL = 1, SEW 8/16/32), without a VLMAX-preservation check.
A request with an illegal vtype that reaches `m_vpu_csr` shall be ignored: vsew and vl are unchanged and the current vl is returned.
`m_vpu_lsu` shall sample `i_mem_ack` only in WAIT, so the memory side (`m_vpu_top`/DMEM path) shall answer at least 1 cycle after `o_mem_req` rises.

The scalar write-back valid for a vector instruction shall be the done pulse AND `o_resp_rd_valid`, so write-back occurs in the cycle the stall releases, with `o_rd_data` passed through from `o_resp_rd_data`.
`m_cpu_dec` shall assert the vector-valid signal only for a legal, unflushed instruction, and the stalled pipeline shall keep the instruction and rs1/rs2 stable until the done pulse.
A VPU access to an address outside DMEM shall be acknowledged immediately, a read returns 0, a write is ignored and no error is raised.

A SEW-dependent vector instruction (`vadd`, `vsra`, `vmax`, `vmv`, `vnclip`, `vwmul`, `vwredsum`) shall be illegal until a legal `vsetvli`/`vsetivli` has been accepted (the shadow SEW is invalid after reset); `vle`/`vse` shall not be checked against vtype.

parameters.name: PARA_VLEN
parameters.description: Vector register width in bits; sets the width of o_mem_wr_data, i_mem_rd_data, o_mem_byte_en, the DMEM row and VLMAX; no port is added or removed.

parameters.name: PARA_LANE_COUNT
parameters.description: Number of parallel m_vpu_lane instances; sets passes per instruction.

constraints.description: PARA_LANE_COUNT is a power of 2 from 1 to 8.
PARA_VLEN is divisible by PARA_LANE_COUNT x LPARA_LANE_W (LPARA_LANE_W = 32).

modules.name: m_soc_top
modules.description: Structural top of the MNIST inference SoC.

modules.name: m_rst_sync
modules.description: Reset synchronizer: async assert, synchronous release (2-flop).

modules.name: m_cpu_top
modules.description: Structural CPU wrapper: 5-stage RV32I+Zmmul pipeline with vector dispatch.

modules.name: m_pc_gen
modules.description: Program counter generation and fetch redirect/halt.

modules.name: m_cpu_dec
modules.description: ID-stage decoder: RV32I/Zmmul/Zve32x subset decode and illegal detection.

modules.name: m_regfile
modules.description: 32x32 register file with write-to-read bypass; x0 = 0.

modules.name: m_lsu
modules.description: Scalar load/store unit with misaligned handling.

modules.name: m_hazard_unit
modules.description: Forwarding, load-use bubble, stall and flush control.

modules.name: m_vpu_dispatch
modules.description: CPU-to-VPU command passthrough and write-back valid.

modules.name: m_vpu_if
modules.description: VPU command interface; latches instruction and operands.

modules.name: m_vpu_dec
modules.description: VPU vsetvli decode: new vl, SEW and scalar result.

modules.name: m_vpu_ctrl
modules.description: VPU control FSM (IDLE, DEC, RD, EXEC, WB, DONE).

modules.name: m_vpu_lsu
modules.description: VPU memory FSM (IDLE, REQ, WAIT, DONE).

modules.name: m_soc_bus
modules.description: Address decode and CPU/VPU memory mux; MMIO routing.

modules.name: m_host_ld
modules.description: Host load port: DMEM 2:1 mux and IMEM write.

modules.name: m_dmem
modules.description: 256 KB single-port data memory wrapper, PARA_VLEN wide.

modules.name: m_apb_master
modules.description: APB4 requester for MMIO accesses; pulses sts.err on PSLVERR.
